description: MeteoEye is the meteorological satellite data access service of Geoinformation Systems, an enterprise of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus. Its receiving station takes images from the AQUA, Suomi NPP, Fengyun, Metop and NOAA satellites 24 hours a day, in 15 to 30 passes a day, and the service has an API for integration with other software, a Russian and English interface, tools to search and filter data, and data download and ordering. The page lists uses such as studying cloud cover and precipitation intensity, improving weather forecasts, monitoring some emergencies and modelling wildfire spread and flood zones, measuring aerosols and assessing air quality, observing ice movement and temperature, monitoring crops, and obtaining air temperature, humidity and greenhouse gas profiles. The same company runs a thermal anomaly service and a search and order service for high-resolution archive imagery. Access is through a login, with ordering; no prices or licence are stated on the page read. Caveats: the station's coverage area and archive depth are not given on the page. Coverage is Belarus and the region seen by the station. It supports hazard exposure analysis for wildfire, flood and ice around infrastructure; the related record is NASA FIRMS active fire data.
